reading:
The judges love this line's numeral law above everything: the day numeral in its waypoint ring on the route, the same light 300 numeral leading its row, and ringed once in its month cell ("the best comprehension device", "a superb joining device"). They also love the readout strip as the welcome's foot (interaction: "the best at-a-glance page"; usability: "the best glanceable Home"), the lit Now-to-Next leg, the pool under 'plan.', the Status needle sheet, the engraved rule heads with stacked units, square ticks and the shape law. In 14a, taking the main camp's frames (rule heads, head rows, the Ready foot) onto the tour's grammar made Waypoint, Ruled first in heat b at 7.7/7.88 linked, in all 8 top fours, with the lowest green share measured (43%). It sits in a four-way tie with Trued, Desk and Sill, so the next gain has to come from what every lens marked:
(1) The empty ~150px right column beside Coming up. All eight lenses named it, and it is the round's shared sin ("ground left empty beside a list").
(2) Ideas, the weakest page: two columns of confetti-coloured squares (the squares break "square = yours"), no scan line, the Status filter lost, and the Kind keys wrapping to two rows (style, system, interaction, type, usability, skeptic).
(3) The phone puts the readout strip above the box, when the question must lead to the field (system, usability).
(4) The Plans month has arcs and dotted stubs inside the cells (usability, skeptic, ledger X14a-19: "ring the days, draw the route above").
(5) Amber is spent three times on one late state on To do (system), and 'Was due' is capitalised, with a mono date making a third style in one cell (type).
(6) Row titles are underlined at rest (interaction).
(7) The tube is small and off to one side (soul).
(8) The title is shared word for word with Plate (style, soul, the skeptic, and the lessons' convergence warning).
To win it should close those with content rather than stretching anything. That means wiring its lit tube to the row it reports (the round's strongest graft pattern: Desk's patch lead, Listing's stem, Departures' wire, all from the main camp or taken by it), and turning Ideas into an instrument page with real data (by road and the heading from home). It must keep its signature (rings carrying numerals) so it does not converge on the rail-and-NOW look the field now shares, and it should bring back tube light only on the lit path: the pool, the readout's lit cells, the tube, the Now-to-Next leg and the wire.

briefs.name: Waypoint, Patched
briefs.hypothesis: Waypoint, Ruled won heat b on its numeral law plus the main camp's frames. Every lens then docked it for the same three things: an empty column beside Coming up, a confetti Ideas page and a phone that hides the box. This cross keeps the instrument intact and fills each hole with something real. The Next up tube moves into the empty column beside Coming up, larger, and a short lit patch lead (Desk Terminal, Patched's best graft, here drawn short and straight as the lessons' failed reach 3 asks) joins it to the Next row it reports. The readout becomes a vertical annunciator stack in the hero's freed right column. Ideas becomes a one-column flight log with by-road figures and a heading arrow (Folio's facts column, rebuilt on the numeral law). The month rings its days and keeps the route above the grid (Dessau's month). Light runs only along the path from Now to Next: tube, lead, leg, the readout's lit cells and the pool under the lit word. That answers the owner's ask to bring the tube's light back without glare, and it answers principle 1 of the lessons (light is wired to what it reports).
briefs.brief:
Start from x14a-waypoint-cross (copy /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/cross/x14b-b/variants/x14a-waypoint-cross/ and its palette json). Keep the palette tokens (--bone, --lead, --route, --route-flown, --steel, --steel-cap, --caution, --plot, --glass, the kind tokens) and the type scale (--fs-label to --fs-title, --fs-num 2.5rem). Keep #6dff9c only on: the mark, Send and primary keys, the lit word, focus, live lamps, the tube, the Now-to-Next leg and the new patch lead.

HOME (templates/home.html, sheet.css):
1. Hero, left column (about 46rem): the 'Vera' eyebrow with her screen (presence) stays. Set the greeting in --plate (IBM Plex Sans Condensed) 600 at --fs-ask (clamp to 3rem, 48px), so the page has one display face with the rule heads (type). It holds one line at 1265px and two clean lines on a phone. The title is 'Send Vera anything to plan.' with 'plan.' in E1 lit-word (the two-layer halo from phosphor_kit.md), full stop inside the lit run, over the existing pool (E7 greeting-glow, scanlines at 4% under the word only). Then the box (E4 box-glow on focus) and the three starters.
2. Hero, right column (about 22rem; the tube's old place): the readout becomes a vertical annunciator stack, `.readout.stack`. Five rows, each 52px, with a 1px --groove between: a label in --code at --fs-label in --lead, a dotted leader (1px, rgb of --lead at 0.35, thinner than now, as system asked), and the figure in Plex Sans 300 tabular at 1.75rem in --bone. The rows are Today (lit: E20 breathing lamp plus the date in --code, phosphor at 'normal' strength with E14 scanline mask on this cell only), Plans 4, To do 4, ▲ Late 3 (the figure in --caution with --caution-glow, the cell's lit mask in amber at half strength), and Ideas 12. Every figure is an <a> (usability): Plans → /plans, To do → /tasks, Late → /tasks?show=open&late=1 or /tasks#late if the view has no param (say which in the notes), Ideas → /ideas. Hover gives a steel afterglow (E9). The stack's top edge carries an E8 edge-light hairline. This replaces the horizontal strip, so the hero ends at the starters' baseline and nothing sits under it.
3. The setup line stays as is, but its lamp is steel, not amber (skeptic, carried).
4. Coming up: the rule head (bone lead, 'Coming up', '4 plans · All plans →') runs full width. Below it, a two-column grid `.coming.patched`: grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) 26rem; gap: 3rem.
   - Left: the route SVG (unchanged drawing: Now tick, Next ring lit with the leg, the ringed numerals 9, 17, 24 on bone arcs, week ticks) is redrawn to the column's width, and the four rows sit under it (numeral 300 at --fs-num, month and day stacked, time in --code, title, relative). Row titles drop the underline at rest; on :hover and :focus-visible an underline in --steel-cap appears with the E9 afterglow (interaction). Drop the dotted leader inside the rows, so the relative column sits at the row's end with no long empty run. The Google note moves under the last row as the band's foot, at --fs-small in --lead, beside the plug icon.
   - Right: the Next up tube (the existing `crt` + `radar` macro, NEXT UP inverse plate, title, 'Sunday 4 October, 13:00', [IN 2 DAYS], '3 more on the radar') moves here from the hero, larger: 26rem wide by about 15rem, the radar at 9rem with full E17 (sweep afterglow, glowing blips), E13 glass bloom and a third of a pixel of blur, E14 scanlines and corner falloff, and E12's case with its power light lit (soul: 'make the tube larger, put the dot on the tube itself'). Its top aligns with the route's axis, so it shows on the first screen at 1265x900.
   - THE PATCH LEAD (graft A): a socket on the tube case's left side (a 10px --steel ring with a lit 4px core, E21) at the vertical centre of the Next row. From it, one straight 2px #6dff9c line runs left across the 3rem gap into a matching socket ring at the end of the Next row's relative text ('Next · in 2 days'). It carries `filter: drop-shadow(0 0 3px rgb(109 255 156 / .6))` and a 6px bloom, and nothing else lights. Drawn as `.coming.patched .next-row::after` (line) and `::before` (socket), positioned by a `--lead-y` custom property as Desk does. It never crosses text, and there is no right-angle jog. Under 64rem it is not drawn.
5. To do and Lately added stay side by side under rule heads.
   - To do: remove the amber 3px row edge. Keep the ▲ triangle and lowercase 'was due 5 days ago' in --caution (system: three signals → two). The square ticks and the NOW track with its lit node stay.
   - Lately added: replace the confetti square bullets with a 3px x 1.1em kind bar in the kind's token at 70% (system: 'kind colour on a bar'; a square is 'yours' under the shape law), the kind's icon unboxed in --lead, title, and 'Activity · for Maya, Theo' at --fs-small. The newest row's bar is lit (its one lamp, per soul's rule 'give each section one lamp').
   - The kids' wishes stays a rule head with its per-kid figures.
6. Phone (max-width 40rem): the order is eyebrow, title, box with Send, starters, then the readout stack as a 2x3 grid (Today full width, then Plans/To do, Late/Ideas), then Coming up: route, tube at full width and 11rem tall with no lead, then rows (system, usability, interaction).

STATUS FOOT (graft B), every page, templates/base.html and _ui.html: the tube's Ready chin plate goes. One 44px line above the footer, `.status-foot`: a live lamp (E20), 'Ready' in bone 600, '· OpenAI · gpt-6-luna' in --code --lead, '· $0.00 of $2.00 today' in tabular Plex, and 'Status →' flush right. The shape key ('○ lit  □ yours  — the page  ▲ needs a look') moves into the right end of the site footer on one line, once, no longer a strip of its own (skeptic: one legend per site).

IDEAS (templates/ideas.html, graft C):
- Head row unchanged: 'Ideas 12', stacked 'ideas / last added Sun 27 Sep', with the date in Plex Sans tabular at --fs-label, not mono. 'Add an idea' is primary.
- Rack sized to content (system), one row of filters:
  - Kind keys as one nowrap latched segment with smaller padding (0.35rem 0.6rem), scrolling inside the rack with a fade mask at the right edge if it overflows.
  - Status as latched keys: 'Any but dropped · Planned · Done · Dropped' (usability: give back the planned/done filter).
  - For as a select.
  - Search and its key.
- The radar tube stays to the right of the rack at full E17 strength.
- The list becomes ONE column, a flight log `.log.idea-grid`, with column heads in --code --fs-label --lead: '#', 'Idea', 'Kind', 'For', 'By road', 'Heading'.
  - '#' in --code --lead.
  - Title: Plex 600, --fs-body, no underline at rest.
  - Kind: the bar plus icon plus word.
  - For: in --ink-2.
  - By road: the drive time set as the numeral law's light figure, Plex Sans 300 tabular at 1.75rem in --bone, right aligned, with 'h' superscript and 'min' at --fs-label.
  - Heading: a 12px bone chevron rotated to the real bearing from home (N 0deg, NE 45deg ... from the compass word already in row.away) beside the letters in --code.
  - The nearest row's figure is lit (its one lamp).
  - Row height 56px on 1px --groove hairlines.
  This is real data on a straight line, as the lessons' failed reach 1 asks; nothing is plotted on a bearing it does not have.

PLANS month (templates/plans_month.html, graft D):
- The head row 'Plans 4 still to come / to 1 Nov' stays.
- The route is drawn ONCE in a strip above the grid, the same SVG as Home's: Now, the lit leg, the Next ring lit, then the 9, 17 and 24 rings, across the grid's full width, with week ticks aligned to the grid's rows' first days where possible. Otherwise it is a four-week strip, with the 'Next · Sun 4 · Oaks Park roller rink' readout at its right.
- Inside the cells: remove every arc, stub and dotted leg (usability, skeptic). A day with a plan rings its numeral: a 1.5px --route ring, Plex 300 at 22px. Today is a filled jewel (--jewel, E21 halo). The Next day's ring is lit #6dff9c with E1 at half strength.
- Under a ringed numeral, a plain chip: a 2px left bar in --route (#6dff9c for Next), the title in Plex 600 at --fs-small, and the time in tabular Plex at --fs-label, not mono.
- Weekend columns keep a faint --slate-them wash (no hatching).

TO DO (templates/tasks.html):
- Drop the amber row edge.
- Lowercase 'was due …', with the date under it in Plex Sans tabular at --fs-label (type).
- Keep the Whose filter, Show segment, 44px Edit keys and the NOW track with its lit node.
- Add the To do head's '▲ 3 late' as a link to the late filter.

SETTINGS: say 'needs a look' once, in the caution line only; drop the head figure's duplicate. Settings cards keep their pictograms, but in --lead, not on tiles.

FORM (idea_form.html, settings_section.html): give it a rule head of its own (bone lead plus 'New idea' / the section name, with 'Back to ideas' at the right) instead of a plain slate panel.

LIGHT CHECKLIST (phosphor_kit.md):
- E1 on 'plan.'
- E2 on the mark
- E3 on Send and the primaries
- E4 on the box
- E5 focus
- E6 top haze at its original 6%
- E7 under the greeting only
- E9 afterglow on row hover
- E12-E14 and E17 on the tube and the Ideas radar
- E14 mask on the readout's two lit cells
- E20 on Today and Ready
- E21 on the rings, the jewel and the patch lead's sockets
Nothing else glows. Keep the page's green share at or under about 45% of saturated pixels: the kind bars (wheat, sage, steel-cyan, clay, rose tokens already in the palette) replace the confetti squares' hue share, so no colour is lost.

briefs.title: 'Send Vera anything to *plan*.' The full stop sits inside the lit run (E1 halo over the existing pool). It is not yet tried: the lessons give 'Give Vera something to plan.' to one line per heat, and Plate holds it in heat b. It says FamilyDB's job: the family hands Vera anything (a weekend, an idea to keep, a reminder, a wish, a calendar question) and the job is planning. It names who hears you, ends on the short lit job word where the eye stops, and as an imperative it cannot be answered 'no' (unlike the failed 'Anything to plan?'). Its verb is the box's own 'Send' key just below, so the label says what pressing does, and it suits the console's transmit voice without making a pun on the motif.
